### application-core values V1 step 1: the interpreter's Strings are UTF-16 code units, as the JVM's

change `lkvnqurnqwwt` · [log `e7462bae943c`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b8c9cad1-a1e9-4dff-af3c-fd39c8035d6f/e7462bae943c2fc14612b7931c07fe16b8926837fa9ce28eafa038792bc45888.jsonl.gz)

The interpreter, which replays every witness, held a String as Rust UTF-8 text, so every isolated surrogate became U+FFFD: "\uD800".equals("\uFFFD") and "\uD800".equals("\uDC00") were true, charAt gave 65533, and a surrogate pair split by substring became two U+FFFD. Now interp::JStr holds a String's and a StringBuilder's code units, and every modelled operation works on them as the JDK's do: StringBuilder.reverse keeps a pair together, indexOf(int) takes a supplementary code point, strip and isBlank use Character.isWhitespace's set, new String(char[]) and its siblings are modelled, append(CharSequence, int, int) is refused instead of appending the whole sequence, and setLength(-1) throws. An operation that needs Unicode's tables (case conversion, equalsIgnoreCase, number syntax) is refused on a String with an isolated surrogate, and Integer.parseInt on any non-ASCII code unit (Character.digit takes every Unicode digit), rather than answered for other text. Messages that quote a String keep its units, and Objects.requireNonNull's message is the very String given. Machine::str_of keeps its signature, now for readers; Machine::units_of is what a String is.

Reproducer first: lib/tests/values.rs, the values stream's model conformance test, runs 67 small String methods (lib/tests/fixtures/values/) on a real JVM and in the interpreter and requires the same code units, or a refusal where one is listed. Before the fix, 28 cases differed and one was refused; now all agree. The full lib suite passes (cargo test: 476 tests, the integration contract application_core.rs included). The audit of what native runs faithfully, two wrong answers found outside V1's core (Character's classification uses Rust's Unicode tables, and a surrogate char renders as U+FFFD in a contract), and an interface request for the merge (the class reader decodes a string literal lossily) are in the brief's Progress. Next: the own checker's bounded Strings.
